newsitem.title: UK: EU plans overhaul of agriculture policies - paper.
newsitem.headline: EU plans overhaul of agriculture policies - paper.

text.p: The European Union's executive body plans a radical overhaul of the bloc's Common Agricultural Policy (CAP), Britain's Independent newspaper reported on Wednesday, quoting a leaked draft of the proposals.

The newspaper said farmers would be paid direct income support, rather than the cumbersome and expensive system of artificially high prices and subsidies that has been used for 35 years under the CAP.

"Brussels will next week propose that guaranteed prices for farmers, the cornerstone of the 30 billion pound ($50.83 billion) -a-year CAP, should be slashed by up to 30 percent for the main crops and commodities in the initial phase of the plan, which could ultimately return agriculture to the free market" the Independent said.

It quoted the document as saying: "The (European) Commission considers it indispensable to proceed with further reforms of the CAP... Improved competitiveness will benefit consumers and leave more room for price differentiation in favour of high quality or typical products."
The Independent said the proposals were due to be published next Wednesday as a key plank of Agenda 2000 -- a package of measures to prepare the EU for expansion into Eastern Europe.
The draft called for price cuts to farmers of 20 percent for grain, 10 percent for milk and 30 percent for beef, said the newspaper.
Price cuts would start to take effect from 2000, with some sectors such as grain taking an immediate hit but the steeper beef price cut would be phased in over two years.

The reform, as outlined in the document, involved a shift from indirect price support to direct income aid, channelled principally to the smallest farmers in outlying regions, the newspaper said. ($1=.5902 Pound)
